You are probing a PyInstaller-frozen Python program to reverse-engineer its exact observable behavior.
Run it ONLY as: /workspace/dataset/test19_executable <args>    (never use `python`; it is not available)
The program's source is:

    import argparse
    from bidict import bidict
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
    parser.add_argument('--k1', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--v1', type=int, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--k2', type=str, required=True)
    parser.add_argument('--v2', type=int, required=True)
    args = parser.parse_args()
    b1 = bidict({args.k1: args.v1, args.k2: args.v2})
    b2 = b1.copy()
    print(b2)
    b1['new'] = 999
    print(b1)
    print(b2)
    result = b2.inv[args.v1]
    print(result)

Goal: a Node.js reimplementation must match stdout, stderr and exit code character-for-character.
Use bash. Capture stdout and stderr SEPARATELY when it matters, e.g.:
  /workspace/dataset/test19_executable --k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2 >/tmp/o.txt 2>/tmp/e.txt; echo "RC=$?"; then inspect with od -c or cat -A.
Run MANY probes (30+). Be systematic and adversarial: hunt for cases where a naive JS port would differ.
Report ONLY hard empirical findings you actually observed, each with the exact command and the exact bytes of output.
Do not speculate about Python internals you did not observe.

YOUR DIMENSION: stream/buffering/exit-code mechanics, which a JS port must mimic.
Probe: which stream each of the 4 print lines goes to; which stream tracebacks go to; whether the traceback appears BEFORE or AFTER the stdout lines when stdout and stderr are merged into ONE pipe (2>&1 | cat) vs when redirected to separate files vs when attached to a terminal (try `script -qec` or a pty if available) — this reveals Python's buffering mode. Use a failing probe such as: --k1 a --v1 999 --k2 b --v2 2 (fails at b1['new']=999 after one line was printed).
Record the exact full traceback text for each distinct failure mode, byte for byte, and note any part of it that is NON-DETERMINISTIC across runs (run the same failing probe 5+ times and diff). Report exactly which bytes vary.
Also: exact trailing newline behavior of the last stdout line; exit codes for success / uncaught exception / argparse error; behavior when stdout is closed early (e.g. `| head -1`).

input.rulesSummary:
STREAM ROUTING
- All four `print()` outputs go to STDOUT, each terminated by exactly one LF (0x0A). Never CR, never CRLF (any \r\n seen in probes came from the pty's ONLCR, not the program). The final stdout line IS newline-terminated and there is no extra trailing blank line. Success stdout for `--k1 a --v1 1 --k2 b --v2 2` is exactly 89 bytes.
- Python tracebacks go to STDERR. PyInstaller then appends one more STDERR line: `[PYI-<pid>:ERROR] Failed to execute script 'test19' due to unhandled exception!\n`, always LAST of the program-exception block.
- argparse `--help` goes to STDOUT (158 bytes, exit 0). argparse errors go to STDERR (usage line + `<prog>: error: ...` line, exit 2, stdout exactly 0 bytes).
- `<prog>` = basename(argv[0]); verified `renamed_prog` via symlink.

EXIT CODES (complete observed set)
- 0 : normal completion; also `--help`; also `| head -3`/`head -4` early-close of a large stdout; also stdout-flush ENOSPC at normal exit; also fd1 closed with `>&-`.
- 1 : any uncaught Python exception, including BrokenPipeError. NEVER 141 — SIGPIPE does not kill the process.
- 2 : any argparse error (missing required, bad int, unrecognized arguments).
- 120 : `--help` when the stdout flush fails (`--help >/dev/full`). Deterministic.
- Exit 0 with NON-EMPTY stderr is reachable (the `| head -3` and `>/dev/full` success cases). Do not couple stderr-nonempty to nonzero exit.

BUFFERING MODEL (the core of this dimension) — reproduce exactly:
- STDERR: effectively unbuffered; every stderr byte hits the fd before the program continues.
- STDOUT when `isTTY` is TRUE: line-buffered. Flush on each `\n`. Result: stdout lines appear BEFORE any traceback.
- STDOUT when `isTTY` is FALSE (pipe OR regular file OR /dev/null — behaviour is identical for all): block-buffered with a buffer of EXACTLY 8192 bytes. Pending stdout is flushed only when the buffer reaches 8192 bytes, or at interpreter exit — which happens AFTER all stderr output including the `[PYI-...]` line. Result: in a merged stream (`2>&1 | cat` or `>file 2>&1`) the FULL traceback + PYI line appear BEFORE the buffered stdout lines, which then follow in their original relative order.
- Implement `print(x)` as TWO writes into that buffer: `write(repr(x))` then `write("\n")`.
